field_001: A browser-based speaking assessment interface created by Wayland Chin to organize randomized prompts, timing, and examiner flow.
field_005: A browser-based examiner interface that combines randomized prompts, timing, and a three-part assessment flow.
field_007: One-to-one speaking assessments require an examiner to listen carefully while also managing questions, timing, and transitions. Printed question sheets add handling, repeat the same visible prompts, and make the process more dependent on each examiner's personal workflow.
field_009: I built a focused web application for the Pre-Intermediate speaking exam. It displays one large prompt at a time, tracks elapsed time, selects another prompt without immediately repeating the previous one, and moves the examiner through Parts A, B, and C. At the end of Part C, one action resets the application for the next student.
field_013: The timer begins and Part A opens automatically.
field_016: A large button presents another randomized prompt within the current part.
field_019: The second control advances from A to B to C.
field_022: Finish / New Student returns to Part A and restarts the timer.
field_024: The demonstration below reproduces the deployed examiner interface while replacing the real question with a neutral label. This shows the design without republishing assessment prompts.
field_027: The application is a self-contained HTML, CSS, and JavaScript tool hosted through GitHub Pages. It requires no installation, stores no student information, and can be updated centrally before a new assessment period.
field_029: One prompt at a time: removes visual clutter and helps the examiner maintain eye contact.
field_030: Randomized selection: varies questions while preventing an immediate repeat within each part.
field_031: Elapsed-time display: keeps pacing visible without a separate timer.
field_032: Two-button navigation: limits the examiner's choices to the next prompt or the next assessment part.
field_033: Responsive layout: adapts the same interface to landscape and portrait screens.
field_035: I use the platform to administer approximately 100–125 five-minute assessments each semester. Two other instructors are also confirmed users. Its present reach is limited to the Pre-Intermediate level, and paper-based delivery remains available.
field_036: The platform standardizes prompt presentation, timing visibility, and examiner flow. It does not score students or replace professional judgment, and I have not yet collected comparative reliability or time-saving data.
field_042: Assessment software creates the most value when it removes small operational distractions. A clear, reliable interface helps the examiner devote more attention to listening and evaluating.
